title: New Year's Eve pistol incident that led to arrest
summary: He recounts firing his stepfather's blank pistol at New Year's Eve, coming into 1913, and being grabbed by a detective.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Well, we wasn't thinking about who was the best or anything in those days. We're just glad we could sing together and sound so good. When did you first start to get there? So when I got to the age where I noticed everybody celebrate Christmas and New Year's Eve with pistols, Roman cannons, shotguns, cannons, anything they got in the processions, they shoot it up there, but I didn't know that there was a law against it. See, you can get away with it, all right, see. Well, I kept on finding my stepfather's old mustard .38 gun, you know, and he had them with blanks in it, but mama kept on hiding it when I'd find it. And I heard this in my bosom one night, and he was going down the right for the street singing, my Brazilian beauty, that was an early tune on Amazon, that's where my love was gone, gone, gone. You know, that face would make that run. How old were you living? Twelve. Yeah. And it's New Year's Eve, coming into 1913, see. So, I was all right till a little kid with a little six-shooter on the other side of the street. Dying, dying, dying, celebrating, you know. So they all know I had this pistol, they say. They call me Dippum out there, get him Dippum. So I just told my big one, he said, yo, yo. Everybody was really good. But when I looked around, those two arms was hugging me, Detective A. Oh, Lord.
